scope: Odyssey on-foot suits, weapons, personal-equipment upgrades, engineering modifications, settlement materials, and practical equipment progression used by the Mongrels Field Manual and Ask the Mongrels.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Pick the suit for the job: Maverick for settlement utility and salvage, Dominator for sustained combat, Artemis for exobiology. The Flight Suit is the baseline suit rather than a specialist platform.
details: The Maverick is the settlement-utility suit and carries the Arc Cutter; it is the natural choice for looting, salvage, theft/heist work and general settlement operations.
The Dominator is the combat-focused suit and can carry a second primary weapon in addition to its sidearm.
The Artemis carries the Genetic Sampler and is the specialist exobiology suit.
All three specialist suits can be upgraded through Grades 2-5 and can receive Engineer modifications.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Personal equipment runs G1-G5. Each step adds one Engineer-modification slot: G2=1, G3=2, G4=3, G5=4.
details: The same 1/2/3/4 modification-slot progression applies to suits and handheld weapons from G2 through G5.
Suit grade upgrades also improve core defensive performance such as shield strength/regeneration and resistances.
Weapon grade upgrades improve the weapon's core performance while unlocking additional modification slots.
Upgrade the underlying grade first when possible so you know exactly how many permanent modification slots the finished item will have.

entries.topic: Upgrades at Pioneer Supplies vs Engineer Modifications
entries.ruleOfThumb: Grade upgrades and Engineer modifications are separate systems: increase the item's grade at Pioneer Supplies, then use personal-equipment Engineers for permanent modifications.
details: G2-G5 suit and weapon grade upgrades consume credits plus Odyssey materials.
Personal-equipment Engineer modifications use separate recipes and require access to an Engineer that offers the desired modification.
Engineer unlock and referral requirements vary by Engineer; check the current Engineer database before planning an unlock chain.
Unlike ship engineering, personal equipment does not use the ship Remote Workshop/pinned-blueprint workflow.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Plan Odyssey modifications before installing them. Suit and handheld-weapon modifications are effectively permanent on that item and cannot simply be swapped like ship experimental effects.
details: Do not spend a scarce modification slot on an effect you do not intend to keep.
Pre-modified equipment can be a bargain only when the installed effect fits the final build.
Owning multiple copies of the same suit or weapon is normal when you want different specialized modification sets.
commonMistakes: Installing a convenient early mod and assuming it can be replaced later.
Buying pre-engineered gear solely because it is G3 even though the existing mod is unwanted.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Check Pioneer Supplies before starting a long upgrade grind. Stations can occasionally sell G2/G3 suits or weapons, sometimes with an existing modification, for credits.
details: A useful G3 purchase can skip the G1→G2 and G2→G3 material costs entirely.
Because personal-equipment modifications are permanent, avoid pre-modified items carrying an effect that conflicts with the planned build.
Availability varies by station and individual stock, so treat pre-upgraded gear as an opportunistic shortcut rather than a guaranteed shopping list.

entries.ruleOfThumb: From G1 to G5, each equipment line uses 1/2/4/5 schematics and Manufacturing Instructions across the four upgrade steps, plus increasing quantities of type-specific materials.
details: Suit upgrades use Suit Schematics; weapon upgrades use Weapon Schematics.
Manufacturing Instructions are used throughout G2-G5 personal-equipment upgrades.
Across G2/G3/G4/G5, the schematic and Manufacturing Instruction counts are 1/2/4/5 per step, or 12 total when starting at G1.
The two type-specific material quantities scale 2/5/9/12 per step, or 28 of each across a complete G1→G5 path.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Odyssey engineering materials are a separate on-foot economy commonly grouped as Assets, Goods and Data. Their sources and trading rules are different from ship Raw/Manufactured/Encoded materials.
details: Settlement lockers, containers and rooms supply many Assets and Goods.
Dataports are a major source of Data, and building type strongly affects what can appear.
Mission rewards are an important source for difficult personal-equipment materials.
Do not confuse Odyssey material handling with ship Material Traders; the two systems are separate.

entries.topic: Bartenders, Asset Trading & Fleet-Carrier Material Markets
entries.ruleOfThumb: Regular station bartenders can exchange Odyssey Assets within their matching subcategories; Goods and Data are not handled like ship Material-Trader exchanges. Fleet-carrier bartenders can also host player buy/sell listings for Odyssey materials.
details: Asset exchanges stay within their relevant on-foot subcategory rather than converting freely across every Odyssey item.
Goods and Data often need to be sourced directly from settlements, missions or player-listed fleet-carrier stock.
Fleet-carrier bartender listings can be useful for hard-to-find unlock or modification items, but availability and prices are player-controlled and can change quickly.
Use a live current database when looking for a specific carrier listing.

sources.name: INARA — Example Fleet Carrier bartender market

entries.topic: Settlement Material Sourcing by Building Type
entries.ruleOfThumb: Target the room/building type that can actually spawn the material. Randomly clearing every settlement is much slower than using a current component database to choose likely dataports and lockers.
details: Manufacturing Instructions can appear across several settlement building types and as mission rewards.
Operational Manuals are associated with MED, RES, IND and CMD locations, crashed satellites and mission rewards.
Biometric Data is associated with MED/CMD locations and mission rewards.
Weapon Test Data is associated with CMD locations and mission rewards.
Settlement loot remains probabilistic, so source lists improve your odds but do not guarantee an item on a specific visit.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Thermal is strongest against shields, kinetic is strongest against unshielded armour, plasma is effective against both but has slower projectiles, and explosive weapons trade ammo/handling for splash damage.
details: Takada laser weapons are the thermal family and are well suited to stripping shields.
Karma firearms are kinetic and excel once the target's shield is down.
Manticore plasma weapons provide strong all-round shield/armour damage but demand better projectile leading.
The Karma L-6 is the explosive launcher and is useful for area damage, especially in ground combat zones.
A Dominator can carry two primaries, making thermal+kinetic or other complementary combinations easy to field.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Noise Suppressor is for pressurised environments; Audio Masking is for unpressurised environments. A dedicated stealth weapon may use both if you want quiet operation in either setting.
details: INARA describes Noise Suppressor as reducing weapon sound when fired in pressurised environments.
INARA describes Audio Masking as reducing simulated weapon sound when fired in unpressurised environments.
Do not treat one modification as a universal silencer for every settlement environment.
Because modification slots are permanent and limited, fitting both is a deliberate stealth-specialist choice.

entries.ruleOfThumb: For settlement work, Extra Backpack Capacity is one of the strongest Maverick quality-of-life choices. Night Vision and Quieter Footsteps are common stealth/utility picks; battery, sprint, jump and tracking are playstyle choices.
details: Extra Backpack Capacity doubles the suit's backpack item/component/data capacity.
Quieter Footsteps supports faster stealth movement without relying as heavily on crouching.
Night Vision is broadly useful for dark settlements and planetary surfaces.
Improved Battery Capacity, Increased Sprint Duration, Improved Jump Assist and Enhanced Tracking are all legitimate fourth-slot or alternate-role options.
Treat these as common practical patterns rather than a single mandatory meta build.

entries.ruleOfThumb: For sustained ground combat, common Dominator priorities are Extra Ammo Capacity, Faster Shield Regen, Combat Movement Speed and Improved Battery Capacity. Adjust for your weapon set and engagement style.
details: The Dominator's second primary slot makes it the natural Frontline Solutions / ground-CZ combat platform.
Extra Ammo Capacity reduces resupply trips during long fights.
Faster Shield Regen reduces downtime after taking cover.
Combat Movement Speed improves mobility while aiming, and Improved Battery Capacity extends time between energy resupplies.
Damage Resistance is a valid alternative when raw survivability matters more than one of the utility slots.

sources.name: INARA community — Ground combat loadout example

entries.ruleOfThumb: Artemis engineering should favor exploration quality of life: Improved Battery Capacity, Increased Sprint Duration, Improved Jump Assist and Night Vision are a strong general-purpose combination.
details: The Artemis is primarily an exploration/exobiology suit rather than a combat platform.
Battery capacity helps on long walks and repeated tool use away from the ship/SRV.
Sprint and jump improvements reduce travel friction across rough terrain.
Night Vision helps with biological searches and safe movement in darkness.
Reduced Tool Battery Consumption is an alternative when sampler/tool drain matters more than one of the mobility slots.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Personal-equipment Engineers have their own unlock/referral network and modification specialties. Check the current Engineer list before farming an unlock item because requirements differ by Engineer.
details: Domino Green is a commonly accessible Bubble entry-point Engineer and offers utility modifications such as Extra Backpack Capacity, Enhanced Tracking and Reduced Tool Battery Consumption.
Jude Navarro focuses more heavily on combat-oriented suit/weapon effects such as Extra Ammo Capacity, Damage Resistance, Magazine Size and Reload Speed.
Other Bubble Engineers unlock additional stealth, handling, mobility and weapon effects through referral chains.
Colonia also has personal-equipment Engineers, including broader end-chain access through Yi Shen.
Some Engineer unlocks require selling specific Goods/Data to bartenders or completing specific mission types, so verify the exact current requirement before grinding.
